environmental.acoustic-noise: 51.6 dBA with the 320 W AC supply (datasheet, ISO 7779 at 23 C)
environmental.altitude: up to 3049 m operating (10,000 ft); 4877 m non-operating
environmental.humidity: 10 to 85 percent noncondensing operating; 0 to 95 percent non-operating

features.poe: IEEE 802.3af on the first eight ports, 15.4 W each, up to 18.6 W with enhanced PoE

features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 members over the 128 Gbps backplane; two rear Virtual Chassis ports

management.lcd: 2 lines of 16 characters with Menu and Enter buttons
management.oob: RJ-45 management port on the rear, 100 Mbps full duplex, with link/activity and status lamps
management.usb: one USB port on the rear

performance.switching-capacity: 136 Gbps packet switching, 264 Gbps aggregate, 64-byte packets (datasheet)

physical.datasheet-dimensions: 17.41 x 1.72 x 16.43 in (44.21 x 4.32 x 41.73 cm) W x H x D; the guide's Table 3 is used for the envelope

power.psu-redundancy: one supply carries a fully loaded chassis; a second gives redundancy (datasheet)

configs.description: EX4200-48T as shipped - one 320 W AC power supply in slot 0 with a cover panel over slot 1, the fan tray, and the uplink slot covered. Side-to-rear airflow. The datasheet also orders the Trade Agreements Act build EX4200-48T-TAA, the same hardware.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: EX4200-48T-DC - one 190 W DC power supply in slot 0 and the fan tray: DC powered, with no PoE (the guide: "EX4200 switches with a DC power supply installed do not provide PoE").
configs.name: dc

configs.description: EX4200-48T-S - the spare chassis, shipped with no power supply and no fan tray: "Power supplies for this model are not shipped by default; you must order them separately", and so is the fan tray. The supply and fan bays are shown open.
configs.name: s

gaps.wanted: A straight-on photograph of the rear. The maker's image library returned 404 for every EX4200 address tried, so the rear is read off the low-resolution callout figure and the supply and fan art follows the isometric drawings.

A straight-on studio photograph of the front. The datasheet's photographs are perspective views from above, so the vertical positions carry a 4.5 percent foreshortening and every front position is estimated.

What the -DC build prints on its model plate. The guide shows the same front for it and the datasheet photographs are of the PoE builds. Because the build gives no PoE, the `dc` face is drawn without the "8PoE" legend and with white numerals; the "EX4200" line is kept.
Where the two-hole protective earthing terminal sits on the side panel and its hole pitch; the guide names it on a side panel and draws no side elevation.
The bracket positions of the front, centre and rear mounting and of the 2-in-recess brackets: no figure in the guide measures them, so no ear position or kit is listed.
A library component for an LCD display; the LCD panel is a decor rectangle until one exists.
The EX-UM-4SFP, EX-UM-2X4SFP, EX-UM-2X4SFP-M and EX-UM-2XFP uplink modules and their ports, left for a later uplink-module slice; the bay takes only the cover panel here.
The fan tray's power draw: neither the guide nor the datasheet states it.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 4 bays (front 1, rear 3); `physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: Guide, Airflow Direction in the EX4200 Switch Chassis and Figure 16: the fan tray "provides side-to-rear chassis cooling"; the datasheet gives 20.3 cfm. The chassis airflow enumeration has no side-to-rear, so `side` is written, the nearest answer; there is no back-to-front build and no handle colour to follow.

chassis.note: Guide Table 3: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm) = 44.45 mm; width 17.25 in (43.82 cm) = 438.2 mm, "19 in. (48.2 cm) with mounting brackets attached", so 438.2 is the body between the bracket flanges; depth 17 in (43.18 cm) with no supply, with the 320 W AC supply or with the 190 W DC supply, and 19.25 in (48.9 cm) with a 600 W or 930 W AC supply (they extend 2.25 in). This model ships with the 320 W supply, so the modelled depth is 431.8 mm. THE DATASHEET DISAGREES: it gives 17.41 x 1.72 x 16.43 in (44.21 x 4.32 x 41.73 cm) and 18.8 in (47.8 cm) with the 600 W or 930 W supply. They are different measures of the same chassis (the datasheet's width is the desktop width and its figures are 0.16 in wider, 0.03 in lower and 0.57 in shallower), and the hardware guide is the newer and the more specific document, so the guide's figures are used; the datasheet's are in attrs. 1RU.

colour.note: The datasheet photograph shows a black face with a navy top strip: the strip reads #191f32 (median of 800 px) and the lower plate #504e57 where a highlight crosses it. The face is drawn #2b2f3d, between the two. The supply and fan faces are a tone lighter and are estimated; no photograph of the rear is held.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's packing list ships two mounting brackets and eight screws, and the guide says the switch mounts on two posts with those, on four posts with the separately orderable four-post rack-mount kit (datasheet EX-4PST-RMK), recessed 2 in from the front with the 2-in-recess front brackets of that kit, on a desk on its rubber feet, or on a wall with the separately orderable wall-mount kit (EX-WMK); the datasheet also lists EX-RMK. The brackets align "along the front, rear, or center of the side panels", and the guide's four-post notes give the rack depths for flush (27.5 to 30.5 in) and 2-in-recess (29.5 to 32.5 in) mounting. No figure dimensions the bracket positions, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. The kit part numbers are recorded here for the later dedupe.

front-ports.note: 48 jacks in two stacked rows, four blocks of six columns. Read off the datasheet photograph at 2.04 px per mm, with the face's left edge at 0: the dark cavities of the top row are centred at 15.8, 30.0, 43.9, 57.8, 71.7 and 85.5 mm in the first block and 104.0 in the second, and the first column of the third and fourth blocks sit at 191.7 and 279.3 mm. The column pitch is 13.94, the registry's 13.97 ganged-jack pitch (0.550 in); the blocks start 88.0 mm apart, so the gutter is 88.0 - 6 x 13.97 = 4.2 mm. Row centres read 16.8 and 31.6 mm down, a 14.8 step, the same step as the EX4300. The top row is the same part turned 180 so that its keyway is up: the photograph shows the lamp windows of the top row at the top and those of the bottom row at the bottom. The last column ends at 356 mm and the plate is bare to the right-hand block. The 24-port figure carries the first two blocks only, then a bare plate.

front-right.note: Read off the 48-port datasheet photograph at 2.04 px per mm across and 1.95 px per mm up from the bottom edge, and checked against the 24F photograph (which reads the same positions within 1.5 mm, the LCD centre at 15.05 and 15.2 mm): the raised right-hand module panel 362.5 to 438.2 mm; the LCD window 375.5 to 411.2 x 10.3 to 19.9 mm (35.7 x 9.6); the Menu button centre (420.7, 12.5) and the Enter button (420.7, 20.7), 6.1 mm across; the three chassis lamps at x 427.8, y 9.05, 12.85 and 16.75; a face screw each side at (366.5, 22.0) and (429.9, 22.0); the uplink slot 366.9 to 429.9 x 26.5 to 41.0 mm. The model plate (296.5 to 344.0 x 0.9 to 5.0 mm) carries "EX4200" centred at 304.5 and the PoE count centred at 334.3. The top strip also carries the Juniper logo at the left, 6.4 to 22.2 x 1.0 to 5.1 mm, reserved as a logo zone and not drawn.

fru-bays.note: Two power supply bays (slot 0, slot 1) and one fan tray bay, each seating the guide's FRU parts. "EX4200 switches have an internal redundant power supply, making the power supply in EX4200 switches fully redundant": one supply carries a fully loaded chassis (datasheet) and a second is for redundancy. The cover panel the guide ships for an empty supply slot is seated in slot 1 as shipped and the supply in slot 0. The guide says mixing AC and DC supplies in one chassis is not supported; that is left to the configurations, since a bay lists every part it can take and a configuration seats a matching set. The fan tray and the supplies are FRUs, hot-swappable; nothing is built into the chassis.

gate-1-front.note: The datasheet photograph of the 48-port switch (page 6, bottom row) is a perspective view from above and a little front-on. Its face spans 894 px across for the guide's 438.2 mm (2.04 px per mm) and 87 px down for 44.45 mm (1.95 px per mm): 4.5 percent shorter than orthographic. So columns, which run across, are read at 2.04 px per mm, and heights are read at the face's own 1.95 px per mm counted up from the bottom edge, which is the edge every photograph shows cleanly. The photographs of the 48P and 24F views (3.2 and 2.05 px per mm) give the right-hand block to within a millimetre, which is the second image the figures are checked against. The guide's own figure of the 48-port front (Figure 1, g020081) is 565 px wide in the PDF and gives counts and order only.

gate-1-rear.note: Guide Figure 4 (g020084, 609 x 252 px as embedded) is a rear view with the top face in perspective: the chassis outline is 557 px across for 438.2 mm (1.271 px per mm) and its face is 53.7 px high for 44.45 mm, so it is 5 percent foreshortened vertically. Positions across are read at 1.271 px per mm and heights at 0.828 mm per px, from the top edge of the face. It is a low resolution raster, so every rear position is good to about 2 mm. Figure 4 is shared by all the EX4200 models: "The rear panel of all the EX4200 switches except EX4200-24F-S and EX4200-48T-S switches are similar."

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. The guide's examples name the network ports ge-0/0/0 and up (it says to connect a console to "port 0 (ge-0/0/0)"), the uplink module's ports ge-0/1/0 and up, and the Virtual Chassis ports vcp-0 and vcp-1. No table gives the numbering rule for every model, so the names stay out of the file as a block and go here.

lamp-legends.note: drawing-vs-photo: guide Figures 5 and 9 print ALM, SYS and MST beside the three lamps, to their right, with a bracket. The datasheet photograph resolves a dark vertical bar at the right of the lamps and cannot resolve type of that size (1.4 mm against 2.04 px per mm, while the 2.2 mm numerals resolve), so it neither confirms nor contradicts the drawing. The legends are drawn as the guide draws them. The order top to bottom is the guide's order of naming (ALM, SYS, MST).

lcd.note: The LCD panel shows two lines of 16 characters (guide, LCD Panel in EX4200 Switches). It is drawn as the green window the photograph shows; no library component exists for a display and none is added, so it is a decor rectangle and not a part. A dark strip above the window, visible on the photograph, is not drawn.

lifecycle.note: Searched on 2026-10-23. Juniper's own milestones page was not reachable; third-party trackers (eol.network, parkplacetechnologies.com, relutech.com, serviceexpress.com) and resellers give an end-of-life announcement of 2019-02-01 for the EX2200, EX3300, EX4200, EX4500 and EX4550, last order 2019-06-30 and last day of support 2024-06-30; two trackers give earlier dates of 2013 for the EX4200-24P and -48P bundles. The 2019 dates are written, from a tracker and not from the maker.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat: the guide's figures show them in perspective with mounting holes in the sides and a protective earthing terminal on a side panel. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

poe-numerals.note: The photographs print the numerals of the PoE ports in orange and the others in white: on the 8-PoE views (EX4200-24T and -48T) ports 0 to 7 are orange, on the 24-PoE and 48-PoE views every numeral is orange. The model plate at the right of the top strip prints "EX4200" in white and the PoE count ("8PoE", "24PoE", "48PoE", or "24SFP" on the fibre model) in orange. This device is drawn as the 8-PoE view shows it. The -DC build carries no PoE (guide Table 1, pp. 4-5; datasheet Table 1: 0 PoE ports), so the `ac` configuration places the "8PoE" legend and the orange numerals as two small parts with `only-in`, and `dc` places white numerals and no legend. No source shows the -DC face itself; see the gaps.

port-lamps.note: Guide, Network Port LEDs in EX4200 Switches, Figure 11 and Tables 7 and 8: each 10/100/1000BASE-T port has two lamps, a Link/Activity lamp (green, blinking with activity, steady when linked) and a Status lamp whose meaning is chosen with the LCD Enter button (ADM, DPX, POE or SPD). The lamps are the jack housing's two corner windows (common/rj45-ganged-eth) and carry that component's default vocabulary. Figure 11 puts the Link/Activity lamp at the left window and Status at the right of the upper jack, which is the component's convention for an unrotated jack and the photograph's for the top row turned 180 with its keyway up; no source pairs the windows of the lower row, so the pairing is the component's.

port-numbering.note: The photograph prints the numbers in pairs above the top row of each column: 0 and 1 over the first column, 2 and 3 over the second, up to 46 and 47 over the last, the even number set higher and the odd lower and to its right. The even number belongs to the upper jack and the odd to the lower, so numbering runs down each column and then across, as on the EX4300. The numerals are 2.2 mm high on the photograph and are drawn at 2.2 mm type, estimated. The pair is read at 2.1 mm left (even) and 0.7 to 1.3 mm right (odd) of the column centre; it is drawn 2.2 mm either side of it, because a mark that lands within 2 mm of the centre of the jack it names reads to lint as a slip at centring. The guide's CLI interface names (ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47) are not printed on the metal and are not modelled; the photograph prints no block legends.

power.note: Guide Table 9: the 320 W supply of this model leaves a 130 W PoE budget for its 8 PoE ports, at up to 15.4 W each (up to 18.6 W with enhanced PoE from Junos OS 11.1). The guide and the datasheet give no typical or maximum draw of the switch itself.

psu-seating.note: Guide, Power Supply in EX4200 Switches and Table 1 (the supply is "Power Supply (Minimum)"): the 320 W AC supply is the minimum for the 8-PoE and fibre models, 600 W for the EX4200-24P and 930 W for the EX4200-48P; "EX4200-24PX and EX4200-48PX switches work only with the power supplies labeled EX-PWR2-930-AC or EX-PWR3-930-AC", and "All EX4200 switches support EX-PWR2-930-AC and EX-PWR3-930-AC". The guide does not say in so many words that a larger supply is accepted in place of the minimum, so this model's bays take the supplies at or above its minimum and the 190 W DC supply the -DC build ships with, and a configuration seats the one shipped.

rear.note: Guide Figure 4, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing: the fan tray plate from 0.6 to 245.6 mm and 2.7 to 26.9 mm down (honeycomb band, thumbscrew at each end); on the chassis below it VCP-0 at 18.9 to 55.1 x 29.6 to 37.9 and VCP-1 at 67.9 to 103.9, the USB port at 121.6 to 136.4, the temperature shutdown lamp centred at (145.3, 35.2), the management jack at 153.7 to 170.0, the console jack at 180.5 to 195.8 and the ESD point centred at (218.0, 36.2); power supply slot 1 from 249.8 and slot 0 from 340.5, each 90.0 mm wide and 41.5 mm high from 2.5 mm down. The figure labels the left supply "Power Supply 1" and the right "Power Supply 0". The small round screws between the Virtual Chassis ports and beside the USB port are not named by any callout and are not drawn.

rear-ground.note: The protective earthing terminal is on the SIDE PANEL (Figure 4's callout "Protective earthing terminal (on side panel)"; the guide's Table 38 lists the location for the EX Series), a two-hole terminal. No figure gives its position or hole pitch, so the side faces carry an `empty` sentence and it is a gap. The ESD point on the rear is modelled.

rear-legends.note: Guide Figure 10 draws the management jack with the letters M, G, M, T stacked upright to its right and the legends VCP-0 and VCP-1 under the Virtual Chassis ports; Figure 4 draws a similar vertical legend beside the console jack that is too small to read. The management legend is drawn as the word MGMT turned to read top to bottom (the library's form for printing that runs sideways, where the figure stacks upright letters), the VCP legends as printed, and the console legend as the turned word CON, an estimate of the unreadable one. The guide names the port "Console port" in its callouts.

rear-temperature-lamp.note: Guide, Rear Panel of an EX4200 Switch: "Temperature shutdown LED", lit when the system shuts down because the chassis temperature has risen above the permitted level (Airflow Direction in the EX4200 Switch Chassis). No colour is stated.

rear-vcp.note: Two Virtual Chassis ports (VCP-0 and VCP-1), "68-pin connector" (guide, Virtual Chassis Ports Connector Pinout Information), joined with the Virtual Chassis cable that ships with the switch (datasheet: 128 Gbps backplane, up to 10 switches). The guide's Table 1 and the datasheet do not give a connector name; the library's VHDCI receptacle is another shape, so a part of the family (juniper/ex4200-vcp-port) is drawn from Figure 4's 36.2 x 8.3 mm opening.

The guide's front and rear figures are isometric drawings and the datasheet photographs are perspective views from above, so every position is a measurement of a projection and is estimated, as the entries below say.

uplink-slot.note: Every EX4200 has one front-panel uplink module slot, under a flip-up door held by screws; "Uplink modules are not part of the standard package and must be ordered separately", and the packing list ships an uplink module cover panel (the blanking panel under the door), preinstalled. The slot is a bay that takes the cover here. THE MODULES ARE NOT MODELLED, by the task's rule: the guide names four, EX-UM-4SFP (4 SFP ports), EX-UM-2X4SFP (2 SFP+ ports, or 4 SFP in 1-gigabit mode), EX-UM-2X4SFP-M (the same with MACsec) and EX-UM-2XFP (2 XFP ports), and the datasheet orders them under those names. The datasheet photographs show the slot with modules fitted (SFP and XFP), so they give the opening and not the cover.
